literature_structure.carotenoid_axis: carotenoids produce yellow petal colour; absence contributes the white/pink side
literature_structure.anthocyanin_axis: anthocyanins produce pink pigmentation whose intensity and distribution across the petal lamina may vary greatly
literature_structure.critical_observation_rule: the source literature treats flowers displaying any pink pigment as pink or bronze despite variation in anthocyanin intensity/distribution

sources.citation: Strauss et al. 2004, Journal of Ecology

consequence_for_image_pipeline.rejected_rule: assign Raphanus morph from whichever fixed palette colour occupies the largest fraction of the ROI
consequence_for_image_pipeline.reason: a pale pink flower may contain large near-white petal area while still being anthocyanin-positive; dominant white pixel area therefore does not imply the white morph

continuous_features_to_retain.anthocyanin_visual_evidence: pink + magenta + purple + red + bronze palette fractions

consequence_for_image_pipeline.thresholds: not set from the six-image pilot
consequence_for_image_pipeline.calibration_plan: estimate whether the two visual pigment axes show separable groups using the full 80-photo calibration set; only then freeze a mapping to white/yellow/pink/bronze for held-out evaluation

pilot_v2_interpretation.resolution: do not tune a threshold to this image; reject direct palette argmax as the biological classifier and retain its continuous pigment-axis features for calibration
